CatalogView.description:
What a tenant's roles may be: the built-in ones, and what a custom one may hold.

It has each built-in role and where it is granted, the actions a custom role may hold, and
where one may be granted. The deployment's roles, an operator's and the application's, are
granted apart from any tenant, and aren't in it.
CatalogView.title: CatalogView

Check.description: One question for ``/checks``: may the caller take this action on this resource?

DeploymentTenantCreated.description:
A tenant was created: the deployment's record of it, beside the tenant's own.

Its entry is in no tenant's log, the deployment's, and names who created the tenant, so an
operator who isn't a member of the tenant it created is seen to have created it. The owner is
a user's id, never an email.
DeploymentTenantCreated.title: DeploymentTenantCreated

get.description:
The deployment's audit log: its operators, granted and revoked.

``type`` keeps only some types of entry, and ``actor_kind``, ``actor`` and ``workspace``
one subject's changes. It reads the window ``after_seq < seq < before_seq``: the first
``limit``, or the last ``last``, oldest first; a client pages back with ``last`` and its
oldest entry's ``seq`` as ``before_seq``.

get.description: Every setting as it is narrowed on a tenant: each layer, the ceiling, the outcome.

put.description:
Narrow a setting on a tenant, or unset it with null.

`If-Match` names the version of the tenant's setting the caller read, `"0"` for one never
set: another is refused with 409; omitted, the last write wins. A value wider than the
layer above is refused with 422, saying how wide it may be and which layer says so. A
caller who may not is refused with 403 before its body or `If-Match` is read.
